va_escape_room_the.blurb: The Escape Room is a compact sandstone crag along the Prospectors trail at Breaks Interstate Park in southwest Virginia. Ten routes, seven of them bolted sport lines and three trad, run from 5.7 up to a single 5.11, with about half sitting in the 5.10 range and a pair each at 5.7 and 5.9. The lines are on the short side and the wall stays in the shade, which suits warm days. It is a handy stop for a climber working along the Prospectors cliff line who wants moderate to mid-grade pitches without a long day committed to one wall.

va_business_time_crag.blurb: Business Time Crag is a shaded little alcove on the Prospectors trail at Breaks Interstate Park in southwest Virginia, close to the state line. All ten routes are bolted sport climbs on sandstone, running from 5.6 to 5.10, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.9 range and just one at 5.10. That spread makes it a friendly spot for newer leaders and anyone wanting a relaxed warm-up or an easy day on moderate lines. The shade helps in summer heat. It is a recent addition to the park, so expect fresher routes than on the older walls nearby.

va_igr_east_side.blurb: The east side is the main wall at Indian Graves Ridge, a walk-in crag in the northern Shenandoah Valley of Virginia. It holds ten routes, a mix of trad (seven) and sport (three), from 5.6 to a lone 5.12, with three at 5.9 and a couple at 5.11. Cliffs here are modest in height, roughly 25 to 35 feet, and most lines finish at bolted anchors, so a walk-off around the north end is also an option. The rock is decent quality, and the long hike in tends to keep the crowds away. Expect to carry both a rack and quickdraws.

va_lover_s_boulder.blurb: Lover's Boulder sits on the Nature Loop at Grayson County Recreation Park in southwest Virginia, a short walk down the trail from the Great Wall of Grayson. It is a long wall of roughly 15 feet with easier lowball climbing toward the left and steeper, harder moves to the right. Ten problems range from V0 to V6, mostly V1 to V2, with a few V5 and a V6 for stronger climbers. The landings are good and there is enough space for a group to spread out and share pads, which makes it a pleasant stop on a day at the park.

va_best_boulder_in_charlottesville.blurb: This is a single boulder in a shallow wooded valley below a ridge near Charlottesville, reached on foot from the Ragged Mountain dam area. It carries ten bouldering problems, V0 up to V5. About four are V5, two or three sit at V4 to V3, and a few easier lines at V0 to V2 round things out. That makes it better for climbers who already boulder in the V3 to V5 range than for beginners, though the lower grades give a warm-up. Come with a pad and a spotter, and bring a way to find the faint game trail in.
